items.title: Teenage boy charged with murder of Victorian girl Layla Jeffery
items.description: The town of Donald in Victoria's west is in mourning, after remains believed to be missing 13-year-old Layla Jeffery were found by police on Thursday.

items.title: Instagram pulls new AI feature after widespread backlash
items.description: The automatic feature, integrated into its Meta AI chatbot, let users edit generated images directly through sketches.

items.title: Speedboat capsize off Vietnam's Phu Quoc island kills 15 tourists
items.description: A tourist boat returning from an island trip in southern Vietnam has capsized, killing 15 Indian visitors, state media has reported.

items.title: NYT reporters subpoenaed over Air Force One security concerns stories
items.description: The Trump administration has issued subpoenas to several New York Times journalists after its report this week on security concerns involving the new Air Force One, according to the paper.

items.title: Australian man dies in Bali while awaiting deportation
items.description: An Australian man has died in a Bali immigration detention centre while awaiting deportation.

items.title: 'Restraining order needed': The fight between Trump and former ally Meloni
items.description: Falling out with Donald Trump is not a situation most world leaders want to find themselves in, but for Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, a spat with the US president could end up playing well for her.

items.title: Iran's supreme leader pledges revenge for father's death
items.description: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has said that avenging his father was "the demand of the nation" and "must certainly" take place.

items.title: 'You might be next': Indonesians react to tech giant's controversial jail sentence
items.description: The sentencing of tech entrepreneur Nadiem Makarim leaves many young Indonesians questioning whether investing in their country could expose them to legal risks.

items.title: That's life: Derryn Hinch's most memorable media moments
items.description: A man of colourful contradictions, Derryn Hinch was a larger-than-life fixture on Australian radio and television over five decades who died on Friday morning at the age of 82.

items.title: France dominates Wallabies to post historic Test win
items.description: Following a second-half blitz, France scores its fourth straight victory over the Wallabies, triumphing 42-26 in the Nations Championship Test in Brisbane.

items.title: Hardwick clashes with Crows fans, as Cats star's injury timeline revealed
items.description: Damien Hardwick clashes with Crows fans at Adelaide Oval, as Jeremy Cameron's injury timeline is revealed.

items.title: England and Norway fans dash to Miami for World Cup spring break
items.description: As England and Norway prepare to face off in their World Cup quarter-final, their fans are lapping up being in one of the party capitals of the world, making every moment count.

items.title: How a $400K executive university job led to a corruption probe
items.description: Plans to create a new executive position at a time when jobs were being slashed at the University of Wollongong caused deep divisions and sparked an inquiry by the state's corruption watchdog.

items.title: Suspect in former UK MP's murder investigation released
items.description: UK police say the man has been released from custody and is "no longer part of the investigation" into Ann Widdecombe's death.

items.title: This Place: Redbank Ngarindjerri
items.description: A grandfather and daughter in South Australia's Riverland are on a journey to revive culture, connection to country and Ngarrindjeri language for the next generation. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: Hollywood's biggest names can't say no to Nolan
items.description: Christopher Nolan and the cast of the highly anticipated The Odyssey sit down with ABC News Breakfast to talk about the upcoming film.

items.title: The 99-year-old Victorian mechanic on the verge of a world record
items.description: Ray Gloster has been a mechanic for 83 years and counting, and at 99, he might be on the verge of a world record.

items.title: Car maker admits selling wrong year vehicles to 1,200 people
items.description: More than 1,200 customers who bought electric and hybrid cars from Chinese maker BYD will be offered a full refund after the company admitted to selling them vehicles from the wrong year.

items.title: Telstra will face Senate inquiry after nationwide outage
items.description: The telco will face a grilling from politicians about this week's nationwide outage that brought businesses and transport systems into chaos.

items.title: Runner gored at Spain's San Fermin bull run festival
items.description: A runner has been pierced in the face by a horn at the San Fermin bull run festival in Pamplona, in northern Spain.

items.title: Sister of missing Toowoomba mum urges community 'to keep looking'
items.description: Faith Isaacs, the sister of missing Toowoomba mum Jana Armstrong, has thanked the community for their search efforts and encouraged them to keep looking.

items.title: One dead after suspected carbon monoxide poisoning in Mount Gambier
items.description: A 55-year-old has died and three other men have been taken to hospital after a case of suspected carbon monoxide poisoning at a Mount Gambier home in South Australia's south-east.

items.title: Police release video of killer Bradley Murdoch filmed weeks before his death
items.description: In never-before-seen footage of police questioning Bradley John Murdoch in his final weeks, the notorious murderer repeatedly tells officers he "knows nothing" about the location of Peter Falconio's remains.

items.title: Details emerge about 16 children who lived in Ohio 'house of horrors'
items.description: From moving around southern Ohio without leaving a paper trail, to being married when they were teenagers, details are emerging about the Siders family.

items.title: Passenger hospitalised after being partially sucked out of Boeing 737 window
items.description: The man's head and shoulders were reportedly outside the Boeing 737's window before passengers on the Ryanair flight were able to pull him back in.
